discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed in e4a1d88. Live discovery is now wrapped in a 4s `withTimeout`; on timeout (or error) we fall back to the cached inventory, so a provider that accepts the request but never completes model discovery (e.g. Claude Code's indefinitely-waiting control request) can no longer leave the picker's `Promise.all` loading forever. Added a fake-timer test that asserts fallback-to-inventory when live discovery never resolves.

Fixed in 8527c5256. The controller now rolls back the optimistically appended user message (matched by id against the live store snapshot) right after `markSessionWorkingDirMissing`, so the transcript no longer shows a message the server never persisted. Covered by a new controller test.

Fixed in 794286aa7, though with a different mechanism than suggested. Tracing `acpTruncateSessionConversation` shows it performs a persisted `DELETE FROM messages ... WHERE created_timestamp >= ?` — the tail is destroyed server-side, not just dropped from the UI. So restoring the pre-edit `currentMessages` would make the UI show messages the store no longer has, diverging on reload.

Instead, the root cause is closed: `on_truncate_session_conversation` now guards on the stored working dir (`ensure_working_dir_present`) before deleting — covering active-with-deleted-dir sessions that skip the activation guard — and returns the same structured `working_dir_missing` error. `updateMessage` therefore aborts before any destructive step, and its catch now also raises the missing-dir banner. For the residual window (dir vanishing between the accepted truncate and the prompt, two back-to-back server calls), the id-filter fallback intentionally leaves the UI at the truncated prefix, which matches the persisted store — truthful state rather than an illusory restore.

New tests: Rust `test_truncate_conversation_rejects_missing_working_dir` (structured error, conversation unchanged) and a UI controller test asserting the refused-truncate path shows the banner and never mutates messages or prompts.

Fixed in 87478ee. Replay now retries each URI on the current ACP client up to three times with bounded exponential backoff. The client is only marked fully replayed after every URI succeeds; exhausted failures leave it retryable by a later same-client callback, and catch-up is emitted only after a successful subscription.
